title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
text:
All through the long summer the ants worked. They carried grains of wheat and barley from the threshing floors, one by one, and stored them in their nest under the ground. It was slow, hot, dull work, and they kept at it every day while the fields were full.

The grasshopper watched them and laughed. Why toil in such fine weather? He spent his days in the grass, singing and enjoying the sun, and he told the ants they were wasting the best part of the year.

Then autumn passed and winter came. Snow covered the fields, and there was nothing left to eat. The grasshopper, weak with hunger, came to the ants' door and begged them for a little of the grain they had dried and stored.

The ants asked him what he had been doing all summer, when he could have gathered food for himself. He told them he had been too busy singing. Then, the ants answered, since he had sung all summer, he could dance all winter. They shut the door, and the grasshopper went away hungry into the cold.
lesson: Good times do not last, so use them to build reserves. The effort you put in while things are easy is what carries you through the season when they are not.
